newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 60 rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 60 rebels - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces killed about 60 Moslem guerrillas and arrested several more in a sustained attack against a hideout where rebel leaders were attending a congress, an Algerian newspaper said on Saturday.
The attack began last Monday following the massacre of 14 family members in Balil village at Bou Smail area, 40 km (25) miles southwest of Algiers, said El Watan newspaper.

The forces, hunting down the murderers, stumbled on a long tunnel with several exits where the guerrillas from the feared Armed Islamic Group (GIA), equipped with assault rifles, were hiding, the usually well informed newspaper said.
Quoting unnamed sources, El Watan said 30 GIA leaders attended the meeting which may also have drawn GIA's commander, 27-year-old Antar Zouabri.
The group is blamed by the authorities for the massacre of villagers in remote areas, bombings in cities and the killing of leading intellectuals and journalists.

The newspaper said the operation concluded on Friday but it did not say whether GIA leaders, including Zouabri, were still holed up in the tunnel or whether they had fled before the huge operation started.
Between 15 and 20 suspected rebels slaughtered 14 family members in Balili last week, El Watan and Liberte newspapers reported last Sunday.
In a separate incident, a bomb explosion killed a young man and wounded another in the Oued Yaich area in Blida.
Al Khabar newspaper said on Saturday that the bomb exploded on Thursday when the two men arrived home. The device was planted near the victims' door, it said.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting guerrillas against government forces since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which Moslems had taken a commanding lead.
